nodes.label: Customer
nodes.description: The buyer who purchased the order and initiates or receives updates about the return.

nodes.label: Request return
nodes.description: Storefront entry point where a signed-in customer requests a return for delivered items.

nodes.label: Create return
nodes.description: Admin entry point where a merchant creates a return on the customer's behalf.

nodes.label: Merchant
nodes.description: The store operator who can create returns manually and approves refunds above the configured cap.

nodes.label: Return label
nodes.description: The shipping label and instructions handed to the customer once fulfillment approves the return.

nodes.label: Ship items back
nodes.description: The customer posts the parcel back to the warehouse using the provided label.

nodes.label: Receive parcel
nodes.description: Warehouse staff log that the parcel has physically arrived before any refund is considered.

nodes.label: Inspect items
nodes.description: Warehouse staff check the condition of each returned item and record the outcome.

nodes.label: Mark received
nodes.description: The merchant marks the return received in the admin UI, moving it toward a refund decision.

nodes.label: Refund issued
nodes.description: The flow's final artifact: money has left the store's account and reached the customer.

nodes.label: Storefront
nodes.description: Next.js storefront the customer uses to browse, buy, and request a return.

nodes.label: Admin dashboard
nodes.description: React admin dashboard the merchant uses to manage orders, returns, and refunds.

nodes.label: Store API
nodes.description: Public-facing routes the storefront calls; no merchant authentication required.

nodes.label: Admin API
nodes.description: Authenticated routes the admin dashboard calls to manage orders and returns.

nodes.label: Workflow engine
nodes.description: Medusa's workflow engine orchestrates the multi-step return process with retries and rollback.

nodes.label: Order module
nodes.description: Owns order lifecycle state and coordinates the other modules involved in a return.

nodes.label: Return model
nodes.description: The Return record created when a return is requested, holding its items and status.

nodes.label: ReturnItem
nodes.description: One line item on the return record, tracking quantity and reason for a single SKU.

nodes.label: Version bump
nodes.description: Bumped on request and again on receipt, so the order stays consistent under concurrent edits.

nodes.label: Fulfillment module
nodes.description: Owns shipment state, including the return shipment this flow creates.

nodes.label: Return option
nodes.description: Evaluates the fulfillment provider's is_return rule to decide whether a label can be generated.

nodes.label: Fulfillment provider
nodes.description: The external carrier that generates and services the return shipping label.

nodes.label: Inventory module
nodes.description: Adjusts stock levels once returned items are confirmed undamaged and resellable.

nodes.label: Payment module
nodes.description: Owns refund logic and enforces the configured refund cap before money moves.

nodes.label: Payment provider
nodes.description: Stripe issues the refund to the customer's original payment method.

nodes.label: OrderTransaction
nodes.description: The OrderTransaction record created for the refund — the system's ledger entry for the money movement.

nodes.label: Event bus
nodes.description: Redis-backed event bus that decouples the order module from anything reacting to return events.

nodes.label: Notification module
nodes.description: Sends the customer-facing updates that accompany each stage of the return.

nodes.label: Postgres
nodes.description: System of record for orders, returns, inventory, and transactions.

nodes.label: Guest return
nodes.description: A guest-checkout order can request a return with no session, verified by order id and email instead.

nodes.label: Item mismatch
nodes.description: Raised when the items received do not match what the customer declared on the return request.

nodes.label: Damaged quantity
nodes.description: Raised when returned stock is not in resellable condition and must be excluded from restock.

nodes.label: requires_action
nodes.description: A human must intervene before the flow can continue; it does not resolve itself.

nodes.label: Refund exceeds cap
nodes.description: Validates the computed refund amount against the store's configured cap before Stripe is called.

nodes.label: Partially returned
nodes.description: The return covers only some of the order's items, so refund and inventory updates apply to a subset.

nodes.label: Cancel return
nodes.description: The customer or merchant withdraws the return request before the parcel is received.

nodes.label: no_notification
nodes.description: Suppresses the customer notification for this return, e.g. for an internal or test order.

nodes.label: CI pipeline
nodes.description: GitHub Actions runs the test suite on every push and pull request touching the return flow.

nodes.label: Integration tests
nodes.description: Jest integration suites cover the return module's request, receive, and refund paths.

nodes.label: Migrations
nodes.description: Schema changes to the return and transaction tables, applied before the updated code deploys.

notes.content:
# Medusa returns
A customer or merchant opens a return, the warehouse receives and inspects the items, then a refund is issued through Stripe. See the [Medusa return docs](https://docs.medusajs.com/) for the underlying data model.

## Return shipping
Medusa generates the **return label**, the customer ships the parcel back, and the warehouse logs receipt before inspection.

## Inspection
Items are checked by hand against the original order line. Notes:
- condition, not just quantity
- photos attached to the return record
- `inspect` decides the outcome
**Refund exceeds cap** halts the flow — a merchant must approve any refund over the configured limit before Stripe is called.
Consider: should the refund wait until inspection confirms the items are undamaged, or fire as soon as the return is marked received?
Consider: with `no_notification` set, the customer sees no update at all — is silent processing acceptable for every reason code, or only for internal/test orders?
Consider: for a partial return, should inventory and refund proceed per item as each is inspected, or only once the whole return is resolved?
